findings.title: unsubscribe dereferences a possibly nil TopicUser record
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns nil when the user has no topic_users row for the topic, for example when they were emailed via mailing list mode or never visited the topic. The next line then raises NoMethodError on `tu.notification_level`, producing a 500. Use `TopicUser.change`, or create the record when it is missing.

findings.title: State-changing action on a GET request, and a bad toggle
findings.body: A GET request changes the user's notification level, which is a CSRF-style side effect. Mail clients and link scanners that prefetch the URL, and anyone embedding it, will mute the topic. The action also toggles: a user at tracking or watching is lowered to regular, and a user already at regular is muted. Reloading the page or clicking the link twice therefore silently escalates to muted. The action should not be this non-idempotent.

findings.title: `render :show` added to the shared perform_show_response
findings.body: `render :show` was added inside the `format.html` block of `perform_show_response`, which `show` also calls. Previously the implicit render happened. `unsubscribe` has no template of its own, so the explicit render is needed there, but the change affects both actions. Check that `show` is not rendered twice or affected when other code paths reach it.

findings.title: Redirect and guardian handling in unsubscribe
findings.body: The redirect to `unsubscribe_url` when the slug is missing or wrong sends a 301, which browsers cache permanently. The redirect target is built from the topic's absolute URL, which is fine. The route `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` carries no slug, so a user who is not logged in gets `ensure_logged_in`'s error rather than a login flow that returns to the unsubscribe action. For an emailed link this gives a poor experience.

findings.title: `unsubscribe_url` is not passed to the other `unsubscribe_link` users
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` locale string now contains `%{unsubscribe_url}`, but only `send_notification_email` supplies that argument. The digest, and any other mailer that sets `add_unsubscribe_link`, does not pass it. Interpolation then raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument, or the link is left blank. `MessageBuilder#body` and `html_part` are used by every mail with `add_unsubscribe_link`, so those mails can break.

findings.title: Multi-line unsubscribe_link text body
findings.body: The block scalar ends with a trailing newline, and `body` appends it after a `\n`. The text-email layout changes and the footer is now two paragraphs. For emails where `unsubscribe_url` is unset, such as the digest, the interpolation fails (see the other finding). Other locale files that still hold the old single-sentence string will not show the per-topic link.

findings.title: Typo in property name 'stopNotificiationsText'
findings.body: The property name is misspelled as `stopNotificiationsText`. It is used consistently between the controller and the template, so nothing breaks, but it should be fixed now rather than baked into the API.

findings.title: Triple-stash renders a title interpolated into an HTML translation
findings.body: `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` renders unescaped HTML built from `model.fancyTitle`. `fancy_title` is HTML-escaped on the server, so this is probably safe, but the safety depends on that server-side escaping. Because I18n.t does not escape the interpolated value, any path that sets `fancyTitle` from unescaped data would allow XSS.

findings.title: Template path and route naming mismatch
findings.body: The template is at `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which maps to the route `topic.unsubscribe`. The route is registered as the top-level `topicUnsubscribe`, so the matching template would be `topic-unsubscribe` or `topicUnsubscribe`. The page may render blank. The `topic` controller and route naming also need checking.

findings.title: Unrelated route constraint changes
findings.body: The `post_number` constraint was removed from the summary routes, and routes were reordered, with no explanation. The `post_number` constraint was a no-op for those paths, but changes to existing routes in a feature PR add regression risk. The `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` route has to sit before the `t/:slug/:topic_id` catch-alls; this order works but is fragile.

findings.title: No tests for the new unsubscribe controller action or URL
findings.body: The only test change adds an `unsubscribe_url` option in the message builder spec. Nothing covers `TopicsController#unsubscribe`: the nil `TopicUser` case, the toggle between regular and muted, the redirect, or login enforcement. There are also no tests for `Topic#unsubscribe_url` or for the per-topic link in the email body.
